SHANGHAI, March 31.
The Shanghai Times says that the Russian steamer Mongugai is expected to sail to day for Vladivostok, taking 150 White soldiers who have gone over to the Soviet. This movement, which is interpreted as a complete disintegration of the White Monarchist group in the Far East, is headed by Semenoff. Reports reaching the Times state that Semenoff his finally made peace with his White enemies and will return to Russia together with many Whites who have severed their connection with the Diehards, of whom General Gleboff is the leader. The Times adds that the Soviet is apparently taking no chances, for it is reported that they will hold Semenoff's wife and family as hostages.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Later information is that Semenoff is still in Shanghai. He did not embark on the Mongugai, and will not, to go Russia, but to Mongolia, where he will carry on commercial negotiations without interference from the Soviet.-Reuter

label: text
text: In an address before the London Iron and Steel Exchange, Sir Edgar Rees Jones dwelt on foreign competition in steel.

label: text
text: He pointed out that the European and American markets had been steadily closing to British producers, and India, Canada, Australia and South Africa had commenced to produce substantially for their own requirements. Therefore the British steel industry must find new markets in less developed parts of the world.

label: text
text: Tuan Chi-jui telegraphed the following reply to the recent communication from Tang Chi-yao and Chao Heng-ti, advocating the adoption of the provincial federation system:—

label: text
text: “I quite appreciate your proposal for the adoption of the provincial federation system. However, the chief object of the recent political reconstruction efforts has been to enable the aims of the national and provincial constitutions to be realised simultaneously. When I arrived in the capital on November 1, I issued several circular telegrams announcing this, and at the inauguration of the Rehabilitation Conference, I emphatically stated that the adoption of a Provincial Constitution must be encouraged. I think this does not differ greatly from the view you have expressed. Our fellow-countrymen, therefore, must hope that whatever organisation is to draft the new Constitution for the nation will speedily come into being, so as the reconstruction efforts now being made may achieve success. I, however, have referred your telegram to the Conference.”

London, March 31.
Results of the first Labour Budget for the financial year which ended to-day show instead of the estimated deficit of £7,946,000 after taking into account supplementary expenditure, a surplus of £3,658,881 net. The decrease in revenue compared with 1923-4 was £37,733,689, chiefly due to falling off in the customs excise.
